column1: # Testing/HDR/hdr-corpus-manifest.tsv - expected clause 8.7.1 CLASSIFICATION per fixture
# WHY THIS EXISTS SEPARATELY FROM qa-profile-manifest.tsv. That manifest records
# the VALIDATION verdict - valid / warning / noncompliant. It cannot express what
# most of these fixtures were built to pin, because failing clause 8.7.1.1's
# membership conditions does not make a profile invalid: the membership negatives
# validate `valid` and are indistinguishable there. This file records the other
# axis - what icGetHdrProfileInfo() concludes - so that a classifier which
# stopped testing one condition fails a row instead of passing silently.
#   purpose            what the fixture is FOR; the only place a reader learns
#                      why a row's numbers are the numbers
# A value of 0 with a source of "-" means not derivable from the profile, which
# is itself an assertion: the not-Linear case of 8.7.1.4.
# THE display_headroom AND headroom_source COLUMNS ARE GONE, with clause 8.10.5.
# The 23-09-2026 revision deletes HDR display metadata outright - "Physical
# display characterization ... is intentionally out of scope for the HDR
# ColorSpace Profile sub-class" - so there is no display headroom to expect and
# no rule whose provenance to record. HdrHeadroomDcvCrwl and HdrHeadroomDcvDrwl
# existed only to pin rules b) and c) of that clause and are DELETED; so is
# HdrCicp2NoColumns, whose subject was the matrix column tags that a ColorSpace
# THE CORPUS MODELS COLORSPACE-CLASS USAGE ONLY (owner direction, 2026-09-26).
# HdrDisplayMetadata and HdrInputDisplayMeta, which carried the retired
# Display-class shape, are replaced by HdrClassDisplayNegative and
# HdrClassInputNegative: single-attribute deltas of HdrColorSpaceClass with the
# class changed and nothing else.  HagcDisplay is renamed HagcColorSpace.
# HdrVersion5 and HdrPcsLab isolate the two membership terms no row could fail
# on alone.  EVERY membership condition now has at least one negative that
# fails on it and nothing else.
# Floats compare to a relative tolerance of 1e-5, because these are icFloatNumber
# (float, not double) and an exact compare would fail on values like 4,92611.
# ADDING A FIXTURE: add it here AND in Testing/qa-profile-manifest.tsv AND in
# Testing/HDR/mkprofiles.sh/.bat, which is the single source of the build list.
# The test fails on an unlisted profile, so forgetting this file is caught.
